rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
rules.description: Memory operations access outside the intended buffer boundary.
Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.
A read accesses memory before or beyond the valid buffer range.
'alert' should not be used in production code.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.
Recompiling an already compiled part of the DOM can lead to unexpected behavior of directives, performance problems, and memory leaks.
Assigning to the special 'exports' variable only overwrites its value and does not export anything. Such an assignment is hence most likely unintentional.
The body of a control statement should have appropriate indentation to clarify which statements it controls and which ones it does not control.
A comment that contains 'TODO' or similar keywords may indicate code that is incomplete or broken, or it may highlight an ambiguity in the software's specification.
